caseStudy.credits: Built on pret’s pokeemerald, RHH’s pokeemerald-expansion, and Pokabbie’s pokeemerald-rogue. This page describes the Divergence fork; upstream work remains credited to its contributors.

vex.description: The Valk Exclusief app lets hotel guests manage bookings, check in online, use digital room keys, and collect rewards. It is available on iOS and Android.
vex.role: At Valk Digital, I worked across the React Native app and its shared Ruby on Rails backend, from feature development and integrations to testing and delivery.
contributions: Built and maintained app features and integrations with backend services in React Native and TypeScript.
Worked on migrating state management from Redux Saga to Redux Toolkit.
Contributed to Roomserve APIs, database changes, and automated backend tests in Ruby on Rails.
Contributed to app testing, deployments, and ongoing maintenance.
vex.backend: Valk Exclusief and HKTD connect to Roomserve, a shared Ruby on Rails backend. It supports both the guest-facing app and the app used by hotel staff.

overview.summary: Hotel bookings, online check-in, digital room keys, and rewards.
overview.contribution: Mobile app development and Ruby on Rails backend work.

divergence.description: Divergence is my personal Game Boy Advance project written in C. It builds on Pokémon Emerald Rogue, adding my own gameplay systems to its existing codebase.
divergence.role: I’m developing Divergence as my own fork of Pokémon Emerald Rogue. The work involves understanding and extending a substantial existing C codebase, alongside maintaining the tools I use to build and check the game.
contributions: Design and implement custom gameplay systems in C within the existing decompilation-based engine.
Maintain Python development and build tools alongside the game code.
Debug changes in mGBA and add focused regression checks.

overview.summary: A Game Boy Advance project extending Pokémon Emerald Rogue.
overview.contribution: Personal C development, build tooling, and regression checks.

valk-to-go.description: Valk to Go provides self-service shops at Valk Exclusief hotels. The software includes the checkout guests use to pay and a back office for managing the shops.
valk-to-go.role: At Valk Digital, I worked across the stack on the software behind Valk to Go. My involvement spanned the React frontends and the Elixir/Phoenix backend that supports them.
contributions: Built and maintained React interfaces for the checkout and shop-management back office.
Developed and maintained backend functionality and APIs in Elixir/Phoenix.
Contributed to testing, delivery, and maintenance of the existing system.

overview.summary: Self-service hotel shops, checkout systems, and shop management.
overview.contribution: React frontends and Elixir/Phoenix backend development.

hktd.title: HKTD — Housekeeping & technical services
hktd.description: HKTD includes a mobile app for housekeeping and technical services staff at Valk Exclusief hotels, plus a web back office. Staff use the app to view room statuses and tasks, while supervisors use the back office to plan and manage the work.
hktd.role: At Valk Digital, I worked on the React Native app, the React web back office, and the backend that HKTD shares with Valk Exclusief.
contributions: Built and maintained staff-app functionality in React Native and TypeScript.
Developed features for the web back office in React.
Contributed to Roomserve APIs, database changes, and automated backend tests in Ruby on Rails.
Investigated issues, maintained existing behaviour, and contributed to testing and delivery.
hktd.backend: HKTD and Valk Exclusief connect to Roomserve, a shared Ruby on Rails backend. It supports both the staff application and the guest-facing hotel app.

overview.summary: Mobile app for hotel staff and a web back office for planning and managing work.
overview.contribution: React Native app, React back office, and shared Rails backend work.

about.title: About me
about.metaDescription: About Daan van Vugt: software development across mobile and web, making games, producing bass music, and cinema.

biography.introduction: Hi, I’m Daan van Vugt, a software developer with three years of experience building mobile apps and web tools. At <experience>Valk Digital</experience>, I worked across the stack in a small team. Some days I was polishing a hotel booking flow in React Native. Other days I was figuring out how to sync housekeeping tasks after a device came back online or why a back-office page was slow.
biography.approach: My work ranged from interfaces to the APIs and databases behind them. I’m happy moving between frontend and backend, and I tend to leave the code a little easier to work with than I found it, whether that means simplifying a component or adding a test for a bug I just tracked down.
biography.personal: Outside work, I make games, produce bass music in Ableton Live, and love going to the cinema. I’m building <divergence>Divergence</divergence>, a Game Boy Advance project written in C, and designing Phantasm, a tactical autobattler. I can happily spend an evening tweaking a game mechanic, getting a bass sound to sit right in a track, or catching a film on the big screen.
